population.note: FICTIONAL. There are about 276M adults. 30.6% are current users (≈84.5M) and 43.5% have ever used (≈120.1M). Cycling arithmetic: ever 43.5 − current 30.6 = 12.9 pts (≈35.6M) used and are off now. About 16.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (16.0 + 5.0)/43.5 ≈ 48.3% have cycled. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year, with the bone-pause code and gating producing more planned stop-starts. Ever-use rose 3.5 pts (limit 5.1) and current use rose 2.1 (the driver). Growth was slower than in 2032–34 because prices stalled rather than rose, the shortage refugees had already restarted, and new starts were partly offset by gating and tenure stops. Age check: 18–29: 17% × 52M = 8.8M; 30–49: 34% × 92M = 31.3M; 50–64: 44.5% × 61M = 27.1M; 65+: 24.2% × 71M = 17.2M. Total ≈ 84.4M ≈ 30.6%. Income thirds average (33.5 + 31 + 27.3)/3 = 30.6. Bottom-third growth (24.5 → 27.3) comes about half from imports (7.1M → 7.8M) and half from employees vesting into tenure-gated plans. Top-third growth is retatrutide 12 mg, now stocked in retail pharmacies. Of 65+ users, ≈15.7M Medicare users include ≈14.3M aged 65+, and the other ≈2.9M older users pay through retiree plans, cash or imports. The 65+ rise (21 → 24.2%) is still damped because about one in five older ever-users is on a bone pause, a post-NAION stop or a fracture-related stop. The ≈155M never-users are skewed toward under-30s, rural residents of non-expansion states, people with contraindications, and refusers by conviction. Pediatric use is 1.3% of ≈73M ≈ 950k, mostly adolescents 12+. About 2 in 5 children live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it, and in the bottom third that parent is now more likely to be on imports than in the top third.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory terms are unchanged: permanent Part D obesity benefit, $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Medicare pays 18.6% of fills, ≈15.7M users (≈14.3M aged 65+, ≈1.4M disabled under-65): ≈6.8M for diabetes and ≈8.9M for obesity. Obesity-benefit gross: 8.9M × $199 × 12 ≈ $21.3B. Beneficiary copays: 8.9M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.3B, leaving ≈$15.9B to the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 15.7M × $199 × 12 ≈ $37.5B gross. Retatrutide 12 mg is on Part D formularies only by tiering exception, because Lilly will not accept the $199 rate for it on the open formulary. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC use the 90% match and the continuation standard. Medicaid pays 14.6% of fills, ≈12.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $29.4B gross before supplemental rebates. A handful of state problem-gambling funds (Ohio, Pennsylvania) reimburse counselling but not the drug, and none has yet decided on the October 2036 indication.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic oral semaglutide and copies of the 50 mg pill. The import alert on the first US filer's Telangana plant is still in place. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, plus 'research-grade' retatrutide, which is still the base of most US gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 50–80. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. EU, UK and Japan: branded retatrutide launched in 2035, and semaglutide generics are entering the EU as exclusivity lapses country by country. US: no generic. A July 2035 D.D.C. ruling held that the first filer's 180-day exclusivity has not been forfeited while it remediates. Rival filers' mid-2035 settlement dates were contingent on the first filer's launch or forfeiture, so they did not trigger. FDA's appeal is pending at the D.C. Circuit.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: direct-portal maintenance prices did not rise or fall in 2035–36. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide are $249–329; the 50 mg Wegovy pill is $299; oral starter doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are $149–150; retatrutide 12 mg is $449 direct and $1,649 list; amycretin $499; MariTide $549/month-equivalent. PBM net is ≈$195–215. Payer mix of ≈84.5M users: commercial 37.0% (31.3M); Medicare 18.6% (15.7M); Medicaid 14.6% (12.3M); cash/direct 20.6% (17.4M, including ≈5.4M 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 9.2% (7.8M). Sum: 31.3 + 15.7 + 12.3 + 17.4 + 7.8 = 84.5M = 100%. Shares are essentially unchanged from 2034 (status quo). About 88% of covering employers use gated designs, about 38% of those add 6–12-month tenure gates, and after the 2035 tri-agency rule a growing share key premium tiers to verified pharmacy adherence (PDC) as well as kiosk weight. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Routes: ≈41% of users are on daily orals; injectables still dominate the ≥20% loss tier.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide incl. 12 mg; retail-stocked single-dose autoinjector from 2035; launched EU/UK/Japan 2035)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe gambling disorder in adults, as adjunct to counselling (orforglipron/Foundayo low dose, approved Oct 2036)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (≈5.4M subscribers on low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo)
compulsive shopping, sports-betting and 'scroll' compulsion, off-label on the strength of the gambling label
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial read out positive in 2036, no filing yet)

pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple_agonist_30pct driver is met by an existing product in a new form and a launch outside the US, as the rules allow. Retatrutide 12 mg (~28–30% mean loss) was already on the US market. In 2035 Lilly's Lebanon, Indiana fill-finish lines brought a single-dose autoinjector into retail stock, so surgical-grade loss is now available off the shelf at chain pharmacies, at an unchanged $449 direct. Retatrutide launched in the EU, UK and Japan in Mar–Jun 2035. No new triple agonist was filed. The compulsive_behaviour driver: Lilly filed an sNDA in Sep 2035 for low-dose Foundayo in gambling disorder on two 26-week phase 3 trials (UNBET-1/2, begun 2033–34: ~38% vs 21% achieving ≥50% reduction in gambling days). FDA approved it in Oct 2036, 13 months after filing. Its label carries the new class reward-blunting warning. Survodutide's MASH sNDA was approved in 2035. The retatrutide CV outcomes trial is ongoing. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing. Lilly's next-generation orals are still in development and not on the market. Market: US ≈ 76.7M paying users (84.5M − 7.8M imports) × ≈$200 net × 12 ≈ $184B. Ex-US ≈$25B, with branded retatrutide in Europe and Japan offsetting generic erosion. Total ≈$209B.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops; retail retatrutide stocking adds more unsupervised escalation nausea.
Rising in absolute numbers with more 12 mg retatrutide use and a larger 65+ base.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low; gray product confounds reporting.
≈1.9M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained over-50s, and the share is higher in retail retatrutide users without coaching.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in the retatrutide, amycretin and MariTide labels; CMS annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.3M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.3M × ~0.6%/yr × 0.35 excess ≈ 17,400 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. The vertebral tail in cycling postmenopausal women persists. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; private gated plans still not bound by it; DOJ civil case against Novo unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. ≈84.5M users × ~4/100,000 × 0.7 ≈ 2,400 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent monocular loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034, not boxed; MDL consolidated 2035; large fleets do voluntary visual-field checks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the 2036 anhedonia pooled analysis found no suicidality signal either.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. FDA's Mar 2036 pooled analysis of randomised SHAPS data (retatrutide substudies, UNBET-1/2, a semaglutide 50 mg pill substudy) puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at 48 weeks at 9.8% vs 4.1% placebo for 12 mg retatrutide, 6.1% vs 4.0% for high-dose dual/mono agonists, and 4.2% vs 2.9% for low-dose orals (≈1 in 25 users, ≈1 in 75 excess). It is dose-dependent and mostly resolves within 8 weeks of stopping. Applied to ≈10M top-dose users and ≈5.4M low-dose subscribers, that implies roughly 570k + 70k ≈ 640k excess cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Mar 2036 class Warnings and Precautions with the prevalence table, plus a Medication Guide update. 'Calm' brands must show the 'about 1 in 25' line at onboarding. FTC consent orders unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Continuing; tenure-gate separations and the new adherence-tier stops add to gating and bone-pause stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; the Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users, in retail retatrutide users without coaching, and in gray-market users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent readout shows a small lag in bone-mineral accrual (mean BMD z-score about −0.3 at 2 years versus controls) whose adult consequence is unknown. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adolescent labels add a bone-accrual statement (2035); postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈7.8M import/counterfeit users. Poison-centre calls are roughly flat since 2034, with seizures up. There has been no repeat of the 2033 cluster, but two smaller Gulf Coast clusters (≈60 hospitalisations) occurred in 2035.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts expanded to seven exporters; Safe Pens bill still stalled; individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pressed counterfeit 50 mg pills and 'calm' tablets are now the majority of seized product by unit; contents range 0–300% of label.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings, NABP guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use; NAION is a minority cofactor.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concentrated in over-50s cut off by gating, tenure separation or adherence-tier lapses; DEXA cohorts are consistent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance published 2035; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting rise of several bpm at 12 mg; CV outcomes trial ongoing; more unsupervised use since retail stocking.

food_and_beverage.state: About 30% adult use keeps salty snacks down ~4% and confectionery ~5% a year. Two private-equity candy portfolios merged in 2035. Price-tier splitting deepened. Premium 'lean-mass' protein lines sell in Scottsdale Whole Foods-type stores, while discount grocers in Maryvale and Dayton sell 'regain-friendly' calorie-dense packs and cheap shakes. Retail retatrutide created a new category of 'triple-dose support' high-protein, low-volume meals.

alcohol.state: Ninth year of spirits volume decline; beer down; non-alcoholic and single-serve formats hold. Tobacco and vape keep falling, helped by the positive cessation trial.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, spend per cover down ~11% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls are standard. 'Full table' heritage nights and rural value buffets serve off-drug customers.

apparel.state: The 'structured' versus 'cycle' split is now industry standard among national chains. Mid-market brands keep shrinking plus inventory. Resale sized for cycling grows.

fitness.state: Growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains expand, and premium gyms sell 'triple management' memberships to new retail retatrutide users. Qualified staff for older lifters remain the bottleneck.

insurance.state: Employer coverage 63%, about 88% of it gated. After the June 2035 tri-agency rule, adherence-verified premium tiers (pharmacy PDC ≥80% plus a kiosk or connected-scale weight) spread from large self-insured employers to mid-size groups. Pharmacy trend ~+8%, mostly volume, since price stalled. Life insurers price untreated BMI and now ask about anhedonia history on drug.

pharma.state: Volume up ~8%, net price flat. Lilly leads, with retatrutide in retail stock and abroad and Foundayo carrying the new gambling indication. Novo holds share with the 50 mg pill. Amgen grows with MariTide. The US semaglutide generic is still parked, so brand revenue keeps climbing. Gray-market suppliers in India and China keep the parcel trade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, more precisely than before. Retail retatrutide made 30% loss cheap enough for the upper-middle, so extreme leanness alone no longer marks the top. What marks it is retained muscle and a DEXA report: coached retatrutide or MariTide. Untrained retail retatrutide users get a new look, 'triple-thin', gaunt in the face and soft in the arm. The middle carries the soft 'pill body'. The bottom carries visible cycling.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use converges (27.3% bottom vs 33.5% top) while bodies diverge. The demographic most visibly sorted is still women 50–64. In Phoenix, a fall-prevention clinic in Maryvale treats vertebral fractures in cyclers while Scottsdale gyms sell lean-mass guarantees. The national 'structured'/'cycle' apparel split is now the industry's sizing system.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are the norm among users. Sunday full-table dinners and church potlucks persist as heritage and as where off-drug families eat, notably in Memphis and Houston.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list a regimen, and since March some add 'not flat', a joking reference to the anhedonia label. 'Coached' still reads as income. Some couples now compare SHAPS scores.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Assumed managed among the insured. The gambling indication extends the frame from food to wanting in general: appetite, betting and buying are now one prescribable category. The backlash coalition is the same size and now argues against 'prescribing quiet'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since Mar 2036 from pooled randomised data: 12 mg retatrutide 9.8% vs 4.1%; high-dose dual/mono 6.1% vs 4.0%; low-dose orals 4.2% vs 2.9%. Applied to ≈10M top-dose users (≈5.7-pt excess) that is ≈570k, and to ≈5.4M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers (≈1.3-pt excess) ≈70k: ≈640k excess clinically meaningful cases, mostly reversible within 8 weeks of stopping. Counterfeit 'calm' tablets add unmeasured exposure.
interior_life.framing: Feature, side effect and now indication at once. The same reduced wanting is a labelled adverse effect (Mar 2036), the mechanism of an approved gambling treatment (Oct 2036), and the product in 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' subscriptions ($149–199/month), which now print 'about 1 in 25 users may feel less pleasure' under the word calm. One brand's ads turned the number around: '24 in 25 just feel even.'
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' subscriptions sit in lifestyle accounts at most large white-collar employers. Tenure-gated coverage is still 'metabolic tenure'. After the 2035 rule, adherence-verified premium tiers mean pharmacy refill data reach the benefits vendor, and some workers fill prescriptions they don't take to keep the tier. Unions bargain over whether a doctor-advised anhedonia stop counts as non-adherence, and three large contracts now exempt it.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' remains a genre. 'Written unmedicated' became a label line after the anhedonia warning. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing. Sportsbook handle growth slowed in high-uptake states, and operators blame 'the pill' on earnings calls. Two state gaming regulators bar operators from linking self-exclusion pages to telehealth prescribers.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists use the new label table. 'Dose-holiday' weekends are now clinically endorsed for some patients, which clashes with employer adherence tiers that count missed doses. Couples with one partner coached and one on imports remain a counselling staple.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 presidential campaign argues over the parked generic and the stalled prices, and over the tri-agency rule, which the House Freedom Caucus and progressive labour members both attack as 'pharmacy surveillance' for different reasons. The Safe Pens bill is still stalled. Sportsbook lobbyists quietly back gambling-disorder coverage in state problem-gambling funds.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding. It labelled anhedonia with a prevalence table, approved the first compulsion indication on randomised data, added adolescent bone language, approved survodutide for MASH, and appealed the D.D.C. exclusivity ruling. There are still no individual prosecutions and no importation or authentication law. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged: Part D obesity benefit at $199 with a $50 copay; 90% Medicaid match for 31 states plus DC. No individual mandate. No state joined or left.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits conditioning moved from private practice to federal sanction. The June 2035 HHS/DOL/Treasury wellness rule recognises verified pharmacy adherence (PDC) and connected-scale or kiosk weights as 'outcome standards' within the existing 30% surcharge cap. The EEOC accepted them as voluntary if a reasonable alternative is offered. Texas and Florida state-employee plans adopted adherence-verified tiers for 2036. The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, as are the Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules. Refill data, kiosk weights and smart-cap logs now feed both public eligibility and private premiums.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and fleets keep visual-field checks. After the anhedonia label, the FAA issued guidance asking aviation medical examiners to record the dose and SHAPS screening; this is not a disqualification. Army accession is still contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the gray market. Section 232 tariffs remain. The Telangana import alert is still a US–India irritant, sharpened by the D.D.C. ruling, which Indian officials say keeps their firm both blocked and blocking. European retatrutide launch gives Lilly ex-US growth.

events.event: Lilly brings a single-dose retatrutide 12 mg autoinjector into retail pharmacy stock from new Lebanon, Indiana fill-finish lines at an unchanged $449 direct price, and launches retatrutide in the EU and UK the same month, with Japan following in June

HHS, Labor and Treasury finalise a wellness rule recognising pharmacy-verified adherence and connected-scale weights as outcome standards under the 30% premium surcharge cap. Texas and Florida state-employee plans adopt adherence-verified incretin tiers for 2036

A D.C. federal judge rules the first-filer generic semaglutide maker has not forfeited its 180-day exclusivity while remediating its Telangana plant, so rival filers' mid-2035 dates do not trigger. FDA appeals, and Novo and Lilly leave portal prices unchanged
Lilly files to add moderate-to-severe gambling disorder to Foundayo's label, citing two phase 3 trials in which 38% of patients halved their gambling days versus 21% on placebo

FDA adds a class warning for reward blunting and anhedonia to all GLP-1 drug labels with a dose-by-dose prevalence table (9.8% vs 4.1% placebo at the top retatrutide dose; 4.2% vs 2.9% at low oral doses). 'Calm' subscription brands must show 'about 1 in 25' at sign-up

FDA approves Foundayo for gambling disorder as an adjunct to counselling, the first incretin indication for a behavioural compulsion. Telehealth 'craving freedom' brands begin advertising shopping and betting relief within days, under the FTC orders' existing limits

open_tensions: The same reduced wanting is now a labelled harm, an approved treatment and a retail product. ≈5.4M 'calm' subscribers carry an 'about 1 in 25' warning, the gambling label invites off-label use for shopping and screens, and nobody has decided whether employer adherence tiers may penalise a patient who stops because of a labelled adverse effect.

Generic semaglutide is held up by a D.C. Circuit appeal over a remediating first filer while prices stay flat and ≈7.8M Americans use imported or pressed counterfeit product. Safe Pens is still stalled.

The 2035 tri-agency rule lets refill and scale data price premiums for ≈31M commercial users. That makes adherence a condition of affordable coverage just as bone, NAION and anhedonia guidance increasingly advises pauses.

Retail retatrutide widened 30% loss to uncoached users, which accelerates lean-mass loss and heart-rate questions in a Medicare-age population. Medicare blocks it from open formulary at $199 while paying through Part A for ≈17,400 excess hip fractures a year.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays $199/month with a $50 copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer channels.
The FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' marketing for the subscription brands.

prose.headline: Now It's on the Label: The Drug That Dulls Wanting Gets a Warning, a Gambling Approval, and Your Boss Counting Every Refill
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 a little under a third of American adults take an incretin drug, about eighty-four million people. Another thirty-five million have taken one and stopped, many of them for the second or third time. The prices that rose in 2033 have neither fallen nor risen since. In July 2035 a federal judge in Washington ruled that the generic maker holding the first right to launch semaglutide had not lost that right while it repaired its Indian plant. The rivals' settlement dates were written to wait on that company, so they waited too. The FDA appealed. Novo and Lilly left their portal prices exactly where they were, and nobody in Congress found the votes to make them move.

What changed instead is what the drugs are understood to do. In March the FDA put reward blunting on every label in the class, with a table attached. At the highest retatrutide dose about one user in ten reports losing pleasure in things they used to enjoy, against one in twenty-five on placebo. At the low oral doses sold as calm it is about one in twenty-five against one in thirty-five. Most of it lifts within two months of stopping. The subscription brands now have to print that number under the word calm. One of them turned it into a slogan about the twenty-four who feel fine. In October the agency approved low-dose Foundayo for gambling disorder after two trials showed it roughly halved betting days for more patients than placebo did. So the same quieting of desire is a labelled harm in the spring and an approved treatment in the autumn. Telehealth companies understood this faster than anyone. Within days they were advertising relief from shopping and from betting apps, careful as ever to say nothing about anxiety.

The bodies kept sorting. Lilly's new Indiana lines put the thirty-percent triple agonist on ordinary pharmacy shelves in 2035. Surgical-grade loss stopped being a top-tier privilege, and the top moved on to the one thing the shelf cannot sell, which is muscle. Coached users with yearly scans keep their shoulders. Uncoached retail users have a new look that trainers call triple-thin, gaunt in the face and soft in the arm. The middle carries the soft pill body. In west Phoenix and Dayton, women in their fifties who cycled through gates and shortages carry the regain around the waist and the fractures in the spine. National chains now size their clothes on the same lines.

Who pays has not changed. Medicare still pays a fixed $199 with a $50 copay, though it will not put the strongest drug on the open formulary at that price. Thirty-one states and DC still run the continuation standard. Employers still cover about two-thirds of the time, mostly with gates and often only after a year on the job. What changed is that Washington blessed the gates. A June 2035 rule from three federal departments lets employers count pharmacy-verified adherence and connected-scale weights as wellness outcomes under the existing premium surcharge. Texas and Florida put their own state workers on those tiers this year. Refill data now reach benefits vendors as a matter of course. Unions spend bargaining hours arguing that a doctor-ordered stop for a labelled side effect should not cost a worker her premium tier. Three contracts agree.

About eight million people still buy abroad, increasingly as pressed pills rather than vials. Two smaller contamination clusters on the Gulf Coast did not move the authentication bill. Hip fractures from long-term use in older Americans are now around seventeen thousand a year above baseline, billed to the part of Medicare that does not buy the drug. From outside, almost all of it looks like a calmer country.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosa Delgado's shift at the Tolleson distribution centre starts at six, so she takes the pill at four-forty with half a glass of water and sits on the edge of the bed for the thirty minutes. Fourteen months here. She vested in March. The pill costs her a twenty-five-dollar copay now. Before that it was the starter dose from the portal at a hundred forty-nine, and before that nothing.

The bottle cap blinks green. Her husband Ernesto's pens sit on the top fridge shelf, the Hyderabad ones, lot numbers already checked against the Telegram list on her phone.

At lunch the kiosk by the break room asks her to step on. She does. The screen says ON TRACK — TIER 1 and thanks her. Marisol from returns says she skipped three days last month because she felt flat, and HR moved her to Tier 2. Forty dollars more a paycheck. She's filling it anyway now and putting the pills in a sock drawer.

Rosa reads the new leaflet in the car, the one with the table. One in twenty-five. She tries to remember whether she liked things more before. She thinks she liked tamales more. She thinks that may just be fifty-four.

At home her son Danny, nineteen, is on the couch with three betting apps open and the Suns down by eleven. On the TV an ad for Unhooked shows a man setting his phone face-down on a picnic table. Danny doesn't look up.

She almost says something. She puts the leftover chicken in the fridge, beside the pens, and goes to bed at nine.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pressed counterfeit 50 mg pills and 'calm' tablets are now the majority of seized product by unit; contents range 0–300% of label.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the parent had counterfeit tablets as a new, emerging entry two years earlier. A majority-of-seizures claim is asserted with no shown chain, while the import share stays flat at 9.2%.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retail retatrutide made 30% loss cheap enough for the upper-middle, so extreme leanness alone no longer marks the top.
